finalOutput:
The game is complete. `snake_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html` (545 lines, ~16.5 KB) is a single self-contained file with embedded CSS and JavaScript — no external dependencies, just open it in a browser.

**What's implemented:**

- **30×30 grid arena** rendered on an HTML canvas with a dark neon-styled UI
- **Classic snake mechanics** — continuous movement in 4 directions, growth on eating food, game over on wall or self collision (snake-vs-snake collisions also end it for the loser in versus modes)
- **Keyboard controls** — Player 1: Arrow keys; Player 2: WASD (used in Human vs Human)
- **CPU-controlled snake AI** — pathfinding toward food that avoids walls, its own body, and the opponent, with a survival fallback move when the direct path is blocked
- **Three game modes**, selectable from the start menu:
  1. Human vs Human (Arrows vs WASD)
  2. CPU vs Human
  3. CPU vs CPU (watch two AIs battle)
- **Live score display** during gameplay (length/score per snake, color-coded)
- **Start menu** with mode selection and controls reference
- **Game over screen** showing the winner/final scores
- **Keypress restart** — press `R` (or Enter) on the game-over screen to return to the menu / restart

The game loop runs on a fixed tick (`setInterval`), direction changes are queued to prevent 180° reversal exploits, and food spawns only on unoccupied cells.

{"path": "snake_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html", "edit_description": "Create a NEW complete single-file HTML Snake game (embedded CSS + JS, no external dependencies, works by double-clicking the file). Implement ALL of the following precisely:

== LAYOUT / THEME ==
- Dark neon theme, page background near-black (#0b1020), content centered with flexbox.
- Title/header area, a HUD bar above the canvas showing live scores for both snakes and the current mode label.
- Canvas 600x600 px representing a 30x30 grid (CELL = 20). Subtle grid lines drawn on canvas.
- Two absolutely-positioned overlay divs over the canvas: #menu (start menu) and #gameover (game over screen), toggled with a .hidden class. Also a small "PAUSED" indicator overlay/element.

== GAME MODES (chosen on start menu via buttons OR keys 1/2/3) ==
1. "Human vs Human": P1 (green snake) = WASD, P2 (orange snake) = Arrow keys.
2. "CPU vs Human": human controls green snake with WASD or Arrow keys (both key sets work); CPU controls orange snake.
3. "CPU vs CPU": both snakes AI-controlled (spectator mode).

== CORE MECHANICS ==
- Snakes move continuously, one cell per tick, setInterval ~110ms. Four directions; 180° reversal forbidden. Queue exactly one direction change per tick (nextDir applied at tick start) so fast double keypresses can't cause instant self-collision.
- Snake 1 starts length 3 at around (7,14) heading RIGHT; Snake 2 starts length 3 at around (22,14) heading LEFT.
- Exactly one food on grid at a time, spawned on a random cell not occupied by either snake. Drawn as a red apple (circle + tiny stem/highlight).
- Eating food: grow by 1 segment, score +1, spawn new food. Live score in HUD.
- SIMULTANEOUS movement: compute both snakes' next heads first; each snake unshifts its new head and pops its tail unless eating; then resolve collisions. A snake MAY move into a cell the other snake's tail just vacated.
- Death conditions: wall hit, own-body hit, other-snake-body hit. Head-on-head (both new heads on same cell) kills BOTH.
- Game ends when any snake dies. Game over overlay shows "GAME OVER", the result ("Player 1 Wins!" / "Player 2 Wins!" / "CPU Wins!" / "Draw!" — use names appropriate to the mode), final scores, and hint text "Press R to Restart • M for Menu".

== CPU AI ==
- BFS shortest path from the CPU snake's head to the food on the 30x30 grid. Blocked cells: out of bounds, both snakes' bodies (except tail cells that will vacate this tick). Move = first step of the found path.
- If NO path to food exists, survival fallback: among non-reversing safe neighbor moves, pick the one with the largest reachable free area (flood-fill count), i.e. follow open space.
- AI runs for each CPU-controlled snake independently each tick.

== CONTROLS / KEYS ==
- P1: W/A/S/D. P2 in Human vs Human: Arrow keys. In CPU vs Human the human may use WASD or Arrows.
- Start menu: keys 1, 2, 3 pick mode (buttons clickable too).
- Game over: R or Enter = restart same mode instantly; M or Escape = back to start menu.
- Space or P = pause/resume during play, showing PAUSED indicator.
- preventDefault on arrows/space so the page doesn't scroll. Ignore direction keys that would reverse the snake.

== RENDERING (Canvas 2D) ==
- Background #0f172a with faint grid lines.
- Snake segments as rounded rects; head brighter with two eyes oriented by movement direction. P1 green family (#22c55e), P2 orange family (#f59e0b). Slightly darker shade toward tail looks nice.
- HUD updates every tick: e.g. "P1: 3" and "CPU: 5" plus mode name.

== START MENU CONTENT ==
- Big "SNAKE" title, subtitle "30 × 30 Arena — Two Snakes Battle", three buttons ("1 — Human vs Human", "2 — CPU vs Human", "3 — CPU vs CPU"), and a controls legend (P1: WASD · P2: Arrows · Space: Pause · R: Restart).

== CODE QUALITY ==
- All JS inside one <script> at end of body wrapped in an IIFE or DOMContentLoaded; clean state machine: states MENU, PLAYING, PAUSED, GAMEOVER; a reset/start function per mode; no global leaks beyond the IIFE; no console errors; no external assets/fonts (system font stack).
Write the FULL file content."}
